raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

A decode request in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` keeps its KV blocks until every TP worker reports it in `finished_recving`. When its READ stays `PROC`, or it is aborted while its handshake is pending, no report comes, so the blocks leak until restart and no metric moves. This adds a pull-side consumer deadline, `kv_load_timeout`, and passes aborts to the workers so a request with no READ posted releases its blocks right away.

Fixes #59872

## Claims

- An aborted request with no READ posted frees its blocks on the next step. If its handshake completes later, the worker only notifies the producer, so the prefill side still frees its blocks right away.
- A request whose READs are still outstanding after `kv_load_timeout` (default `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl`, 480 s) fails under `kv_load_failure_policy`, logs a `transfer_timeout` failure and counts in `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers`. Its blocks stay allocated until every handle leaves `PROC`, since a released handle can still DMA into them.
- The remote engine stays connected. Releasing it makes NIXL report the stalled READs as `ERR` while they can still write into the blocks (ai-dynamo/nixl#2338), so nothing here frees blocks on that report.
- `kv_load_timeout <= 0` disables the deadline. Push mode is unchanged.

## Validation

New tests in `test_nixl_connector.py` step a real scheduler, `KVOutputAggregator` and CPU pull workers built on the existing `FakeNixlWrapper`, with READs that stay `PROC` until the test resolves them.

```
pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_nixl_connector.py \
  -k "abort_before_read or stalled_read or kv_load_timeout_disabled"
```

| Test | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_abort_before_read_releases_blocks` (2 TP workers) | fails: request stays `FINISHED_ABORTED` holding its blocks | passes |
| `test_stalled_read_fails_request_at_kv_load_timeout` | fails: request stays `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` | passes |
| `test_stalled_read_keeps_blocks_until_it_resolves[timeout]` | fails: request stays `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` | passes |
| `test_stalled_read_keeps_blocks_until_it_resolves[abort]` | passes | passes |
| `test_kv_load_timeout_disabled[0]`, `[-1]` | passes | passes |
| Total | `3 failed, 3 passed` | `6 passed` |

The three cases that pass on `main` guard what this change must keep: blocks of a posted READ stay held until it resolves, and a disabled deadline never fails a READ.

Existing suites, same command on `main` (with the new tests) and on this PR:

| Files | `main` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_nixl_*.py`, `test_multi_connector.py` | `7 failed, 608 passed, 3 skipped` | `4 failed, 611 passed, 3 skipped` |
| `test_remote_prefill_lifecycle.py`, `test_remote_decode_lifecycle.py`, `test_kv_load_failure_recovery.py`, `test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`, `test_output_aggregator.py`, `test_error_propagation.py`, `test_kv_connector_lifecycle.py`, `test_bidirectional_kv_transfer.py`, `test_handshake_pp_aggregation.py` | `73 passed` | `73 passed` |
| `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k "kv or connector or remote"` | `29 failed, 45 passed` | `29 failed, 45 passed` |

On `main` the 7 failures are the 3 new tests plus 4 that fail the same way on both and come from the CPU-only test machine: `test_abort_timeout_on_prefiller[ray]` and `[None]` (no `torch.ops._C.init_cpu_memory_env`, no Ray on CPU), `test_fewer_blocks_with_hma[google/gemma-3-1b-it-512]` and `test_multi_example_connector_consistency` (models not cached, run with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`). The 29 scheduler failures are all EC connector cases, which cannot load their model config with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`. Runs were on macOS with `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu`. `pre-commit run --files <changed files>` and the manual-stage `mypy-3.12` hook pass.

End-to-end on GPUs. Rig: upstream `main` CI image for `5f30fc7031` (`0.30.1rc1.dev619+g5f30fc703`), NIXL 1.4.1 installed as CI does, bundled UCX 1.22.0, `UCX_TLS=rc,cuda_copy,cuda_ipc` over 8 ConnectX RoCE HCAs per node, Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B TP1, prefill engines on one H100 node and the decode on another. The change is applied as an overlay of the installed package. A test-only shim keeps the decode worker's `check_xfer_state` at `PROC` for requests whose id matches a pattern; the data itself transfers normally. Three such requests of about 5,050 prompt tokens each, client timeout 40 s:

| Decode | Stalled requests | `vllm:kv_cache_usage_perc` after they end | `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers` | Later requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | no output until the client gives up at 40 s | 0.0438 for the rest of the run | 0 | ok |
| this PR, `kv_load_timeout: 15` | end at 15.1 s | 0.0438 (handles still `PROC`, blocks held) | +3 | ok |

The blocks stay held because NIXL cannot yet tell when a stalled READ has stopped writing. With NIXL `main` on the same RoCE setup, a 4 GiB READ followed by `invalidateRemoteMD` reports `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` within 0.4 ms and then writes all 4 GiB within 500 ms (ai-dynamo/nixl#2338).

The same shim on a GLM-5.3 P/D deployment (TP2 decode, PCP8 prefill, default `kv_load_timeout`): three stalled requests of about 6,000 prompt tokens failed with HTTP 500 at 481.8 to 482.2 s, and three other requests sent during the stall completed in 1.8 to 2.6 s.

Accuracy, `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/test_accuracy.py` (gsm8k, P/D through `toy_proxy_server.py`, expected 0.41): `main` 0.4147, this change together with the other two NIXL fixes from the same investigation 0.4139. Both pass.

## Details

Root cause: `Scheduler.finish_requests` defers the free of a `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` request until `_update_from_kv_xfer_finished` sees it in `finished_recving` from every worker. A worker reports it only when `_pop_done_transfers` sees all of its handles leave `PROC`, which has no deadline, and the abort never reaches the worker. On a deployment with TP2 decode and PCP8 prefill this left about 11 aborted requests per day on one decode rank, and KV usage reached about 97% with `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers` at 0. Details in #59872.

Abort: `NixlPullConnectorScheduler` tracks the requests it parks in `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS` and sends one in `reqs_to_abort` when it finishes before that report. A worker that has no READ posted for it drops it and reports it in `finished_recving`. Posted READs are left alone, since only their completion says the blocks are no longer written.

Timeout: the deadline is armed when the READs are posted. On expiry the request's blocks go to `_invalid_block_ids`, so under `fail` the scheduler fails the request in the same step and keeps its blocks while the handles are outstanding. Under `recompute` the request is rescheduled only after `finished_recving`, so it never recomputes into blocks a READ can still write.

Why the engine stays connected: on NIXL 1.3.2 through current main, `nixlAgent::getXferStatus` returns `NIXL_ERR_NOT_FOUND` once `invalidateRemoteMD` has dropped the remote section, before the backend `checkXfer` runs, and `check_xfer_state` maps that to `ERR`. So if the worker released the engine, it would see a stalled READ fail right after `remove_remote_agent` and free its blocks. That status says nothing about the DMA: `invalidateRemoteMD` destroys the remote rkeys with the GET possibly outstanding, the backend `disconnect` only drops the connection from `remoteConnMap`, and the request handle keeps a `CONNECTED` endpoint that is closed in flush mode on release. Reclaiming those blocks depends on ai-dynamo/nixl#2338: NIXL stops the outstanding operations by force-closing the endpoint before it releases the remote metadata and rkeys, and reports a terminal status only after that. Until a NIXL release carries it, the blocks of a stalled READ stay quarantined; releasing the engine on timeout can follow once it does. `release_dlist_handle` needs no deferral, since `makeXferReq` copies the descriptors.

Limitations:
- With HMA, invalid block ids are unsupported for more than one KV cache group, so a timed-out request is counted at the deadline and fails only when its handles resolve.
- A timed-out request counts once at the deadline and once per handle that later reports `ERR`, as any failed handle does.
- An aborted request with a READ posted keeps its blocks until the READ completes, fails or hits the deadline.
- The default deadline applies to every pull. A READ outstanding for 480 s is treated as broken.

Stubs built with `object.__new__` in `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/utils.py` and `test_nixl_connector_hma.py` get the new fields.

Not a duplicate. Searched open PRs for `nixl timeout`, `kv_load_timeout`, `WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS`, `nixl abort`, `nixl stuck`, `nixl leak`, `reqs_to_abort`, `delay_free_blocks`, `remote kv load timeout` and `finished_recving abort`. Closest:
- #46289 (open, for the push-mode leak in #46283) frees the blocks from the scheduler after a grace period. With a READ still outstanding that frees blocks a DMA can still write, so this PR frees them only when NIXL reports the handle done, on the pull path.
- #54689 (merged) keeps an engine with in-flight READs from TTL eviction. Its review asked for a timeout on the transfer as a complement, which this is.
- #56104 (merged) fixes the multi-handle release race and notes the same DMA caveat for the error path in `_try_release_xfer_handle`.
- #55471 (open) recovers locally invalidated peer metadata after receive failures. It acts on handles that report `ERR`, and this acts on handles stuck in `PROC`.
- #59524 (open) rolls back incomplete remote-agent handshakes and does not touch recv deadlines or aborts.
- #58004 (open) adds scheduler gauges for KV held by pending transfers, which would show this leak. It does not release anything.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to trace the code paths, write the change and tests, and draft this description.

files.patch:
@@ -132,6 +132,10 @@ python tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py \
     - In bidirectional mode, the decoder caches KV blocks for multi-turn conversations. This TTL controls how long those blocks are held before being released. Unlike the prefiller lease, this TTL is not renewed via heartbeats.
     - Example: `--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector_extra_config": {"decoder_kv_blocks_ttl": 600}}'`
 
+- `kv_load_timeout` (via `kv_connector_extra_config`): Time (in seconds) the decoder waits for the KV reads of one request. (Optional)
+    - Default: the value of `decoder_kv_blocks_ttl` (480)
+    - A request whose reads are still in flight after this time is failed under `kv_load_failure_policy` and counted in `vllm:nixl_num_failed_transfers`. Its KV blocks stay allocated until the reads complete or fail, since an in-flight read can still write to them. Set to 0 or less to disable.
+
 ## Bidirectional KV Transfer (Multi-turn)
 
 In standard disaggregated prefilling, KV cache flows in one direction: Prefill (P) computes the KV cache and Decode (D) reads from P. For multi-turn conversations this is wasteful — D already holds the KV cache corresponding to the generated tokens from prior turns, yet P must recompute it from scratch on every new turn. Bidirectional KV transfer lets P **pull** existing KV blocks from D via RDMA before computing only the new tokens, significantly reducing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) for long-prefill such as **multi-turn heavy scenarios**.

+class _StallingNixlWrapper(FakeNixlWrapper):
+    """READs stay in flight until ``resolve()``."""
+
+    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
+        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
+        self.posted: list[int] = []
+        self.notified: list[bytes] = []
+        self._stalled: set[int] = set()
+
+    def make_prepped_xfer(
+        self,
+        xfer_type: str,
+        local_xfer_side_handle: int,
+        local_block_descs_ids: list[int],
+        remote_xfer_side_handle: int,
+        remote_block_descs_ids: list[int],
+        notif_msg: bytes | None = None,
+    ) -> int:
+        handle = super().make_prepped_xfer(
+            xfer_type,
+            local_xfer_side_handle,
+            local_block_descs_ids,
+            remote_xfer_side_handle,
+            remote_block_descs_ids,
+            notif_msg,
+        )
+        self._stalled.add(handle)
+        self.posted.append(handle)
+        return handle
+
+    def send_notif(self, agent_name: str, notif_msg: bytes) -> None:
+        self.notified.append(notif_msg)
+
+    def resolve(self) -> None:
+        self._stalled.clear()
+
+    def check_xfer_state(self, handle: int) -> str:
+        return "PROC" if handle in self._stalled else "DONE"
+

+class _DecodeHarness:
+    """A decode scheduler and its TP workers, stepped like the engine core."""
+
+    ENGINE_ID = "my-engine-id"
+
+    def __init__(self, make_pull_worker, num_workers: int = 1, **extra_config):
+        vllm_config = create_vllm_config(
+            kv_connector_extra_config={"engine_ttl": 0, **extra_config}
+        )
+        vllm_config.kv_transfer_config.kv_buffer_device = "cpu"
+        self.scheduler = create_scheduler(vllm_config, num_blocks=100)
+        self.workers = [make_pull_worker(vllm_config) for _ in range(num_workers)]
+        self.aggregator = KVOutputAggregator(expected_finished_count=num_workers)
+        self.block_pool = self.scheduler.kv_cache_manager.block_pool
+        self.num_free_blocks = self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    def add_request(self, request_id: int) -> str:
+        request = create_request(
+            request_id=request_id, num_tokens=40, do_remote_prefill=True
+        )
+        assert request.kv_transfer_params is not None
+        request.kv_transfer_params["remote_block_ids"] = ([0, 1, 2],)
+        self.scheduler.add_request(request)
+        return request.request_id
+
+    def connect(self) -> None:
+        """Complete each worker's pending handshake with the remote engine."""
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker._handshake_futures[self.ENGINE_ID].set_result(
+                worker._nixl_handshake("my-host", 1234, 1, self.ENGINE_ID)
+            )
+
+    def step(self) -> None:
+        scheduler_output = self.scheduler.schedule()
+        outputs: list[ModelRunnerOutput | None] = []
+        for worker in self.workers:
+            worker.start_load_kv(copy.deepcopy(scheduler_output.kv_connector_metadata))
+            results = worker.get_transfer_results()
+            outputs.append(
+                ModelRunnerOutput(
+                    req_ids=[],
+                    req_id_to_index={},
+                    kv_connector_output=KVConnectorOutput(
+                        finished_recving=results.finished_recving,
+                        failed_recving=results.failed_recving,
+                        invalid_block_ids=worker.get_block_ids_with_load_errors(),
+                    ),
+                )
+            )
+        output = self.aggregator.aggregate(outputs)
+        assert output is not None
+        self.scheduler.update_from_output(scheduler_output, output)
+
+    def status(self, req_id: str) -> RequestStatus | None:
+        """The request's status while the scheduler holds its blocks."""
+        request = self.scheduler.requests.get(req_id)
+        return request.status if request is not None else None
+
+    def all_blocks_free(self) -> bool:
+        return self.block_pool.get_num_free_blocks() == self.num_free_blocks

+def test_abort_before_read_releases_blocks(make_pull_worker):
+    """An aborted request with no READ posted frees its blocks.
+
+    The scheduler holds the blocks until every worker reports the request in
+    finished_recving, and a worker still waiting on its handshake has nothing
+    else to report it with. A handshake that completes after the abort must
+    not READ into the freed blocks; it only notifies the producer.
+    """
+    harness = _DecodeHarness(make_pull_worker, num_workers=2)
+    req_id = harness.add_request(1)
+    harness.step()
+    assert harness.status(req_id) == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_REMOTE_KVS
+
+    harness.scheduler.finish_requests(req_id, RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED)
+    assert harness.status(req_id) == RequestStatus.FINISHED_ABORTED
+    harness.step()
+    assert harness.status(req_id) is None
+    assert harness.all_blocks_free()
+
+    harness.connect()
+    harness.step()
+    assert not any(worker.nixl_wrapper.posted for worker in harness.workers)
+    for worker in harness.workers:
+        assert worker.nixl_wrapper.notified == [b"prefill-1:1"]

+def test_stalled_read_fails_request_at_kv_load_timeout(make_pull_worker):
+    """A READ outstanding past kv_load_timeout fails its request at once and
+    counts as a failed transfer. The remote engine stays connected."""

+    worker = harness.workers[0]

+    assert _DecodeHarness.ENGINE_ID in worker._remote_agents

+def test_stalled_read_keeps_blocks_until_it_resolves(make_pull_worker, finish):
+    """Blocks a READ may still write to are freed only once it resolves,
+    whether the request was aborted or timed out."""
+    harness = _DecodeHarness(make_pull_worker)
+    wrapper = harness.workers[0].nixl_wrapper
+    req_id = harness.add_request(1)
+    harness.step()
+    harness.connect()
+    harness.step()

+    assert harness.status(req_id) is None
